fullPassage: Vision is influenced by our preconceptions about reality. In viewing a scene, we establish unconscious hierarchies that reflect our functional relationship to objects and our momentary priorities. For example, when visualizing a hammer in our mind's eye, we tend to "see" it in profile or at some other "ready for use" angle. One would probably not visualize a hammer as seen from the top so that the handle is hidden by the hammer's head. The functional relationship we have with objects creates visual expectations that interfere with our ability to see "like a camera." The camera, like the human eye, sees only shapes and colors. It documents the world impartially through a lens that is similar to the eye. When we look at them carefully, photographs are often surprising because they don't interpret confusing details but simply serve them up to us with a mechanical indifference. And because of their flatness, photographs often contain areas that appear as unrecognizable colors and shapes.

❌ ② abandon(버리다) — interfere — impartially: abandon은 '버리다'로 위계를 세운다(establish)는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ establish — assist(돕다) — impartially: assist는 '돕다'로 방해한다(interfere)는 맥락과 반대
❌ ④ establish — interfere — selectively(선별적으로): selectively는 '선별적으로'로 공정하게(impartially) 기록한다는 맥락과 반대

det.korean: (A) profile=옆모습(측면에서 본 형태), (B) profile=인물 소개(약력 기사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 옆모습 — (B) 인물 소개: 측면에서 본 형태와 인물 소개 기사로 정확 ←정답
❌ ② 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 윤곽선/경력은 각 맥락에 부정확
❌ ④ 자세/성격은 두 맥락 모두와 어긋남
det.tip: profile: 옆모습(from the side) / 인물 소개(magazine profile)

questions.passage: When we look at them carefully, photographs are often __________ (surprise) because they don't interpret confusing details but simply serve them up to us. Because of their flatness, photographs often contain areas that appear as unrecognizable colors and shapes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: surprise → surprising: 감정을 유발하는 주체(사진)를 설명하므로 현재분사 형용사
det.analysis: ✅ 정답: surprising (감정을 일으키는 대상 → 현재분사)
det.tip: photographs are surprising → 감정 유발 주체는 -ing

questions.passage: Vision is influenced by our preconceptions about reality. In viewing a scene, we establish unconscious hierarchies that reflect our functional relationship to objects and our momentary priorities. For example, when visualizing a hammer in our mind's eye, we tend to "see" it in profile or at some other "ready for use" angle. One would probably not visualize a hammer as seen from the top so that the handle is hidden by the hammer's head. The functional relationship we have with objects creates visual expectations that interfere with our ability to see "like a camera." The camera, like the human eye, sees only shapes and colors. It documents the world impartially through a lens that is similar to the eye. When we look at them carefully, photographs are often surprising because they don't interpret __________ but simply serve them up to us with a mechanical indifference. And because of their flatness, photographs often contain areas that appear as unrecognizable colors and shapes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사진은 혼란스러운 세부(confusing details)를 해석하지 않고 그대로 보여줌
det.analysis:
❌ ① obvious facts(명백한 사실) — 사진이 있는 그대로 보여준다는 맥락과 어긋남
✅ ② confusing details(혼란스러운 세부) — 해석 없이 그대로 제시한다는 맥락에 정확 ←정답
❌ ③ hidden meanings(숨은 의미) — 사진은 의미를 해석하지 않으므로 부적절
❌ ④ personal opinions(개인적 의견) — 기계적 무관심 맥락과 반대
det.tip: don't interpret confusing details but simply serve them up
